findings.premise: Unfinished stage state lives in the local daemon and an opaque state token, so it cannot be resumed on another machine.
findings.evidence:
The evidence supports what the premise says. Its anchor (src/mcp) is stale.

Supporting: The state token is a short reference into a store on one machine, not a self-contained payload:
- mcp.txt:27 shows "encodeState mints a short URL-safe base64 token (22 chars, no padding)". A token that short cannot carry the folded payload, so it can only point to an entry held elsewhere.
- S001/LLD.md:39 says the token is "realized as a private state-store record, never persisted to LMDB/Lance/DuckDB".
- frame-epic S005/LLD.md:35 says "The token was minted by a prior encodeState/saveState on this server instance and has not expired (TTL) or been released."
- S005/LLD.md:31 and :55 say an unknown token raises StateTokenNotFound, with the messages "server restarted / TTL expired / already completed".
- mcp.txt:32 shows "releaseState drops the entry so a subsequent decodeState fails".

Together these confirm that unfinished stage state lives only in the local daemon's own store, behind an opaque token. Another machine's daemon cannot resolve that token.

Stale anchor: Every match in live source is under src/daemon/steps/*. Examples: src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/types.ts:37/44/50, src/daemon/steps/analyze-step/types.ts:35, and src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/phases/synthesize.ts:139 (inputStateToken). The src/mcp/workflow-step/state.ts path appears only in older LLD/PLAN docs (S005/LLD.md:55, PLAN.md:18). The gathered evidence has no source match under src/mcp. The anchor is out of date but still points at the right concept.
findings.action: Keep the premise. Re-anchor it from src/mcp to the live state-token code under src/daemon/steps: the per-step types.ts files and the step state module or state store, wherever encodeState/decodeState/saveState now live. Then the probe can resolve against current source and not against old design docs.

proposedFix.rationale: The premise is correct according to the evidence: short opaque token, a private store on this server instance that is never persisted, and not-found after a restart or TTL. q425abf90.question: Item a2: One assumption is low confidence (Jira approval can stand in for a signoff request, unverified); how a Jira approval refers to artifact content must be verified at design.
q425abf90.choice: Reference by artifact id + version only
q425abf90.rationale: Jira follows the GitHub pattern: the daemon creates the Epic, Story and Task issues in Jira, as tracker-auto does for GitHub, and writes the Jira issue key back into the artifact record. The binding is the recorded issue key plus the artifact id and version; no content hash for now. The HLD must carry a note on artifact versioning: record which artifact version a Jira signoff request was opened for, and treat a hash or snapshot binding as a later hardening. A git sync (pull or push) also runs a Jira sync that writes Jira status back into the artifact tracker record, as tracker.sync does for GitHub, and the user can trigger the Jira sync explicitly. A failing or slow Jira call never blocks the git operation; it only reports. Completion is still read live from the tracker when a stage is attempted.

body.title: Team signoff and claim-based workflow
body.problem: The insrc workflow assumes a single person working alone. An artifact is approved by one yes from whoever is at the keyboard, so there is no way for the other people on a team to agree before the work moves to its next stage; the only independent check, the other-party review, is between two models and involves no colleague. Nothing records who owns a piece of work, so two people can author or build the same item at once and discover the collision only when their changes meet. Work that is handed from one person to another cannot be picked up, because the state of an unfinished stage lives on one person's machine and in an opaque token. The tracker support is built for one tracker only, so a team that tracks its work and reviews its changes in a different system cannot use it, and the rules a team wants to hold everyone to (which stages need agreement, whether ownership is enforced) have nowhere to live that one developer cannot quietly change for themselves, since settings today are per machine. The cost falls on every team of more than one person: approvals that mean only that one person was satisfied, duplicated or conflicting work, and a chain whose gates the team cannot trust or enforce.

summary.prose: Teams get a workflow where moving to the next stage needs agreement from other people, not just the author, and where each piece of work has exactly one owner at a time. The agreement and ownership live in the tracker the team already uses, so reviewers need not run insrc themselves, and the rules the team sets cannot be loosened on a single machine. A repo that does not opt in works exactly as it does today.

nonGoals.text: No provisional mode: no stage starts before the previous stage's signoff request has completed.
nonGoals.rationale: A blocking gate is simple and safe; tracking which downstream work is stale after an upstream change is a large cost the team did not choose to take on.

nonGoals.text: Team signoff is never called a review and never counts toward the other-party model review; the meaning of model review and local approval is unchanged.
nonGoals.rationale: Three separate layers must stay distinguishable in vocabulary and in code.

nonGoals.text: No partial signoff of a request's contents.
nonGoals.rationale: If reviewers want different outcomes for different artifacts the request is split instead.

nonGoals.text: insrc does not decide who may sign off, how many must, whether bots count, when approvals go stale, or who may override.
nonGoals.rationale: The tracker or code host already owns these rules; duplicating them would drift.

nonGoals.text: No polling or webhooks to detect completion; completion is checked on demand through the tracker.
nonGoals.rationale: Avoids a background service, rate-limit and credential concerns.

nonGoals.text: No direct cloud REST for GitHub or GitLab (command-line tools only; a thin REST client only for Jira), and no enforcement in the AI host's own tracker connectors.
nonGoals.rationale: Enforcement must hold in every host, and connector coverage differs between hosts.

nonGoals.text: No automatic takeover of a stale claim.
nonGoals.rationale: Changing ownership is a person's decision.

nonGoals.text: No shared team daemon or shared index.
nonGoals.rationale: Each developer keeps their own; the repo and tracker are the shared truth.

nonGoals.text: No team policy read from a file in the developer's working tree.
nonGoals.rationale: A locally editable file would let one developer override the team's rules.

nonGoals.text: Building the GitLab and Jira trackers themselves is outside the first delivery; only the common interface they will plug into is in scope.
nonGoals.rationale: GitHub ships first; the interface must make later trackers possible without reworking the gates.

assumptions.text: Workflow artifacts are files committed to the repo, so version control already shares them between developers.
Teams that adopt this already use an external tracker or code host in which assignees, reviewers and approval rules are managed.
The tracker's own permissions and review rules are authoritative, so insrc only needs to know whether a request completed and who the assignee is.

Today the tracker flow creates issues for Epics, Stories and (optionally) Tasks, and looks up an existing issue by label before creating it only for the Epic; Story and Task issues are created without such a lookup, so making their creation safe to repeat is new work.
The terminal client already reads the shared settings catalog definition (through its command bar) but has no per-repo tracker settings screen; its Setup screen covers system and model setup.
Jira has an approval concept that can stand in for a signoff request, but how an approval refers to artifact content is unverified.

A design for a tracker tool with one implementation per tracker type exists; it has passed its daemon review but carries no approval stamp and is not built, and it overlaps this work, so it must be reconciled with the common interface.

constraints.text: Enforcement of signoff and claims lives in the daemon, never in the AI host's connectors.
Tracker adapters are command-line-first with structured output and contract tests; only Jira may use a thin REST client.
The meaning of the other-party model review (meta.review) and of local approval (approvedAt) must not change.
A repo without the policy file must behave exactly as it does today.
Policy is read only from the remote default branch and cannot be overridden locally; configuration is local and per repo.
New settings are defined once in the daemon's shared settings catalog, so that the VS Code settings, the JetBrains settings and the terminal client all present them from one definition.
The daemon owns all database access; clients and the MCP server reach it only through IPC.
A tracker that lacks a capability the policy requires is rejected when loaded; there is no degraded operation.

stories.title: Rely on a tracker only for what it can really do
stories.userValue: A team can rely on a tracker only for things it can really do, and later trackers can be added without weakening the team's gates.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repo whose configured tracker declares every capability the team policy needs
acceptanceCriteria.when: the tracker is loaded
acceptanceCriteria.then: loading succeeds and the team features use only the capabilities the tracker declared

acceptanceCriteria.given: the policy needs a capability that the configured tracker does not declare
acceptanceCriteria.when: the tracker is loaded
acceptanceCriteria.then: loading is refused with an error naming the missing capability, and no reduced mode is run

acceptanceCriteria.given: the tracker behaviour that exists today for GitHub (issues for Epics, Stories and Tasks)
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is reached through the common interface
acceptanceCriteria.then: its results are the same as before

acceptanceCriteria.given: a developer whose machine lacks the tracker's command-line tool or sign-in
acceptanceCriteria.when: the tracker is loaded
acceptanceCriteria.then: the error says which tool or sign-in is missing

functionalRequirements.statement: Every tracker declares which of claim, issue creation, signoff request and completion detection it supports.
functionalRequirements.rationale: The policy can be checked against the declared set.

functionalRequirements.statement: A tracker missing a capability the policy needs is refused at load.
functionalRequirements.rationale: No gate may be silently skipped.

stories.title: Set team rules centrally so no one can override them locally
stories.userValue: A team lead sets which stages need agreement and whether ownership is enforced once, and every developer is held to it.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repo whose remote default branch carries a policy file
acceptanceCriteria.when: any developer runs a workflow action
acceptanceCriteria.then: the policy as it stands on that branch is applied

acceptanceCriteria.given: a developer edits the policy file in their working tree or on a feature branch
acceptanceCriteria.when: workflow actions run
acceptanceCriteria.then: the edit has no effect until it is on the remote default branch

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repo with no policy file
acceptanceCriteria.when: any workflow action runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: behaviour is exactly as before and no team check is made

acceptanceCriteria.given: a team lead in a repo with no policy
acceptanceCriteria.when: they run the team setup command
acceptanceCriteria.then: a starter policy (signoff for definition, high-level design, low-level design and build completion; claims enforced) is written for them to review and commit

acceptanceCriteria.given: the remote default branch cannot be reached
acceptanceCriteria.when: a team action needs the policy
acceptanceCriteria.then: a previously fetched policy is used if one exists, and otherwise the action is refused with the reason

functionalRequirements.statement: The policy names team mode, the stages needing signoff, claim enforcement and the claim units.
functionalRequirements.rationale: These are the rules that must hold for everyone.

functionalRequirements.statement: A repo without a policy is a solo repo.

stories.title: Keep personal tracker settings local and editable from every client
stories.userValue: Each developer sets their own tracker target, tool locations and branch naming from the place they already use, without touching the team's rules.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a developer opens insrc settings in VS Code or JetBrains for a repo
acceptanceCriteria.when: they view the repo's tracker section
acceptanceCriteria.then: they can see and edit the tracker type, target, tool locations and sign-in, and branch naming for that repo

acceptanceCriteria.given: a developer using the terminal client
acceptanceCriteria.when: they open the repo's tracker settings
acceptanceCriteria.then: they can see and edit the same fields they can in VS Code and JetBrains

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repo with no explicit tracker target
acceptanceCriteria.when: the tracker is resolved
acceptanceCriteria.then: the target comes from the repo's git remote

acceptanceCriteria.given: a developer changes a local setting in one client
acceptanceCriteria.when: they open the settings in another client
acceptanceCriteria.then: the same value is shown

acceptanceCriteria.given: team rules set by the policy (such as which stages need signoff)
acceptanceCriteria.when: a developer opens their settings in any client
acceptanceCriteria.then: the rules are shown read-only with the policy's value and cannot be edited there

functionalRequirements.statement: Local settings are per user and per repo and are not shared.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Personal and environment details differ per person.

functionalRequirements.statement: Every client shows the same settings from one definition.

stories.title: Have an issue ready for every piece of work
stories.userValue: Each piece of work has an issue to own, so claims and signoff always have something to attach to.

acceptanceCriteria.given: team mode and an Epic's definition artifact is first drafted
acceptanceCriteria.when: the draft is written
acceptanceCriteria.then: an issue for the Epic stage exists in the tracker, and writing the draft again never creates a second one

acceptanceCriteria.given: team mode and a Story's design artifact is first drafted
acceptanceCriteria.when: the draft is written
acceptanceCriteria.then: an issue for the Story's design stage exists in the tracker, and writing the draft again never creates a second one

acceptanceCriteria.given: team mode and a Story's plan with several build Tasks
acceptanceCriteria.when: the plan is drafted
acceptanceCriteria.then: each build Task has its own issue whatever the local setting for Task issues says, and drafting again never creates a second issue for a Task

acceptanceCriteria.given: the tracker cannot be reached when a draft is first written
acceptanceCriteria.when: the issue cannot be created
acceptanceCriteria.then: the author is told that the stage cannot yet be claimed and why

functionalRequirements.statement: The same stage unit never gets two issues, however often its draft is written.
Task issues are always created in team mode.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Each build Task is a claim unit.

stories.title: Hold a stage by claiming it, and block everyone else from changing it
stories.userValue: Only one person works on a stage at a time, so two people never collide on the same item.

acceptanceCriteria.given: team mode and a stage unit whose issue has no assignee
acceptanceCriteria.when: a developer claims it
acceptanceCriteria.then: they become the assignee in the tracker and can run changing actions on that stage

acceptanceCriteria.given: another developer holds the claim
acceptanceCriteria.when: someone else tries to author a step, build, approve locally or open a signoff request on that stage
acceptanceCriteria.then: the action is refused naming the holder, while analyze and review of that stage still work

acceptanceCriteria.given: an item that was assigned to a developer directly in the tracker
acceptanceCriteria.when: that developer next acts on it
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are recognised as the holder without a separate claim, because the assignee is read from the tracker at every stage turn

acceptanceCriteria.given: a claim held by a developer
acceptanceCriteria.when: the holder or an administrator releases it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the tracker assignee is cleared and others can claim the stage

acceptanceCriteria.given: a claim whose holder has been inactive for a long time
acceptanceCriteria.when: another developer tries to take the stage without a release
acceptanceCriteria.then: the attempt is refused, because claims are never taken over automatically

acceptanceCriteria.given: a stage whose signoff request has completed
acceptanceCriteria.when: the completion is next checked
acceptanceCriteria.then: the claim is released automatically

functionalRequirements.statement: A claim is the assignee of the stage unit's issue, read live.
functionalRequirements.rationale: The tracker stays the source of truth.

functionalRequirements.statement: Claims end only by explicit release or by completion, never by timeout.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Ownership changes by a person's decision.

stories.title: Hand unfinished work to a new owner without losing it
stories.userValue: When work is reassigned, the new owner picks up where the previous one stopped, on their own machine.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a developer mid-way through a stage that is then reassigned to someone else in the tracker
acceptanceCriteria.when: the first developer next tries a changing action
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is refused and they are offered to park their draft

acceptanceCriteria.given: the first developer chooses to park their draft
acceptanceCriteria.when: parking completes
acceptanceCriteria.then: the draft is committed to a handoff branch and a note pointing to it is added to the issue

acceptanceCriteria.given: a parked draft on a handoff branch
acceptanceCriteria.when: the new assignee continues the stage on their own machine
acceptanceCriteria.then: they resume from the parked draft and its progress, without the first developer's machine or session

acceptanceCriteria.given: a developer whose machine is lost before they could park
acceptanceCriteria.when: the new assignee continues the stage
acceptanceCriteria.then: they resume from the latest committed artifact files and redo only the unfinished step

functionalRequirements.statement: A parked draft carries everything needed to resume.
functionalRequirements.rationale: The new owner uses a different daemon.

functionalRequirements.statement: A stage's resumable state can be rebuilt from committed files.

stories.title: Require signoff in the tracker before the next stage starts
stories.userValue: Colleagues agree before work moves on, in the tracker they already use, without needing insrc.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a stage the policy marks as needing signoff, with artifacts that have passed model review and local approval
acceptanceCriteria.when: the claim holder submits them for signoff
acceptanceCriteria.then: a signoff request containing the chosen artifacts is opened in the tracker and linked from the stage's issue

acceptanceCriteria.given: an artifact that has not passed model review or local approval
acceptanceCriteria.when: the holder tries to submit it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the submission is refused saying which prerequisite is missing

acceptanceCriteria.given: a signoff request that has not completed
acceptanceCriteria.when: anyone tries to start the next stage
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is refused, saying the stage awaits signoff and linking the request

acceptanceCriteria.given: the tracker reports the signoff request completed
acceptanceCriteria.when: someone starts the next stage
acceptanceCriteria.then: it proceeds and every artifact in the request is recorded as signed off together

acceptanceCriteria.given: a signoff request containing several artifacts
acceptanceCriteria.when: it completes
acceptanceCriteria.then: all of its artifacts are signed off and none is signed off alone

acceptanceCriteria.given: a stage the policy does not list for signoff
acceptanceCriteria.when: the author approves it locally
acceptanceCriteria.then: the next stage can start as it does today

acceptanceCriteria.given: an artifact that is signed off
acceptanceCriteria.when: its records are shown
acceptanceCriteria.then: model review and local approval appear exactly as before, and signoff is shown separately and never counted as a review

functionalRequirements.statement: Signoff is a gate separate from model review and local approval.
Completion is checked when the next stage is attempted, not in the background.

stories.title: Revise a signoff request after reviewers ask for changes
stories.userValue: Reviewer feedback is handled in one place without weakening the author's own approval.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an open signoff request on which a reviewer asks for changes
acceptanceCriteria.when: the claim holder revises the artifact
acceptanceCriteria.then: local approval must be run again before the revised artifact is pushed to the same request

acceptanceCriteria.given: a revised artifact that has been pushed
acceptanceCriteria.when: the request is checked
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is still the single review thread and an earlier completion does not carry over

acceptanceCriteria.given: someone who does not hold the claim
acceptanceCriteria.when: they try to revise an artifact in an open request
acceptanceCriteria.then: the revision is refused

functionalRequirements.statement: Every change after review feedback passes local approval again.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Merging must mean the same thing the reviewers saw.

openQuestions: Item a2: One assumption is low confidence (Jira approval can stand in for a signoff request, unverified); how a Jira approval refers to artifact content must be verified at design.

Item s1d: The 'one tracker only' part of the problem is only enabled by the common interface, since GitLab and Jira trackers are a stated non-goal. Open items in the plan doc (migration of existing artifacts, a 'my items' view) have no Story yet.

requirements.statement: A stage that the team's policy marks as needing signoff does not let the next stage start until the signoff request for it has completed in the tracker.
requirements.rationale: Signoff is the team's gate to advance, separate from the author's own approval.

requirements.statement: Local approval by the author and the LLM, and the existing other-party model review, keep their present meaning and remain prerequisites to opening a signoff request.
requirements.rationale: The three layers must not be confused: model review, local approval and team signoff.

requirements.statement: One signoff request can cover several artifacts, and its completion signs off every artifact it contains; a request is never partly signed off.
requirements.rationale: The author chooses the grouping and a reviewer decides on the request as a whole.

requirements.statement: Only the current holder of a stage unit's claim can run the actions that change that stage; anyone can still read, analyze and review it.
requirements.rationale: One owner at a time prevents conflicting work on the same item.

requirements.statement: A claim is held by the assignee of the stage unit's tracker issue, is read from the tracker at every stage turn, and an assignment made directly in the tracker is honoured.
requirements.rationale: The tracker stays the source of truth for who owns work.

requirements.statement: A claim ends only by explicit release (by its holder or an administrator) or automatically when the stage's signoff request is seen to have completed; there is no automatic takeover of a stale claim.
requirements.rationale: Ownership never changes hands without a person's decision.

requirements.statement: When a stage is reassigned while in progress, the previous holder is refused further changes and is offered a way to park their draft so the new holder can resume from it.
requirements.rationale: Handoff must not lose unfinished work.

requirements.statement: A stage's unfinished state can be rebuilt from files committed to the repo, so that a different person on a different machine can continue it.
requirements.rationale: Each developer has their own daemon; the repo and the tracker are the shared truth.

requirements.statement: Each stage unit (the Epic's definition and high-level design, a Story's low-level design and plan, and each build Task) gets its own tracker issue automatically when its artifact is first drafted, without ever creating a second issue for the same unit.
requirements.rationale: A claim needs an issue to attach to, and some trackers need the item to exist before work begins.

requirements.statement: Which stages need signoff, whether claims are enforced and what the claim units are is set by a central policy kept in the repo and read from the remote default branch, and cannot be overridden on a developer's machine.
requirements.rationale: The team's rules must hold for everyone.

requirements.statement: Each developer's own settings (which tracker and target, tool binaries and sign-in, branch naming) are local and editable from the VS Code settings, the JetBrains settings and the terminal client.
requirements.rationale: Personal and environment details differ per person and must not be policy.

requirements.statement: The team features reach the tracker only through a common interface that declares what each tracker can do, and a tracker that cannot do something the policy needs is refused when it is loaded.
requirements.rationale: Support for further trackers must not weaken the team's gates.

requirements.statement: A repo with no policy behaves exactly as it does today.
requirements.rationale: Solo use must be unaffected.

requirements.statement: Every tracker declares which of claim, issue creation, signoff request and completion detection it supports.
requirements.rationale: The policy can be checked against the declared set.

requirements.statement: A tracker missing a capability the policy needs is refused at load.
requirements.rationale: No gate may be silently skipped.

requirements.statement: The policy names team mode, the stages needing signoff, claim enforcement and the claim units.
requirements.rationale: These are the rules that must hold for everyone.

requirements.statement: A repo without a policy is a solo repo.
requirements.rationale: Solo use is unaffected.

requirements.statement: Local settings are per user and per repo and are not shared.
requirements.rationale: Personal and environment details differ per person.

requirements.statement: Every client shows the same settings from one definition.
requirements.rationale: Three clients must not drift.

requirements.statement: The same stage unit never gets two issues, however often its draft is written.
requirements.rationale: A duplicate would split ownership.

requirements.statement: Task issues are always created in team mode.
requirements.rationale: Each build Task is a claim unit.

requirements.statement: A claim is the assignee of the stage unit's issue, read live.
requirements.rationale: The tracker stays the source of truth.

requirements.statement: Claims end only by explicit release or by completion, never by timeout.
requirements.rationale: Ownership changes by a person's decision.

requirements.statement: A parked draft carries everything needed to resume.
requirements.rationale: The new owner uses a different daemon.

requirements.statement: A stage's resumable state can be rebuilt from committed files.
requirements.rationale: Local state is not shared.

requirements.statement: Signoff is a gate separate from model review and local approval.
requirements.rationale: Three layers must stay distinct.

requirements.statement: Completion is checked when the next stage is attempted, not in the background.
requirements.rationale: No polling or webhooks.

requirements.statement: Every change after review feedback passes local approval again.
requirements.rationale: Merging must mean the same thing the reviewers saw.

citations.quotedText: ONE tracker tool, with one implementation per tracker type.

citations.ref: User decisions made in the 2026-10-16 brainstorm session, recorded in docs/plans/team-workflow.md
